signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Middle East Escalation
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.555, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 9.356) following reported explosions on two oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. The 1W G10 scorecard shows USD as the top outperformer (+1.660% avg across 9 pairs) while NOK sits as the ultimate laggard (-2.097% avg across 2 pairs), driving an extreme 3.757% leader-to-laggard spread. Fed at 4.00% vs Norges Bank at 4.50% leaves a -50bp nominal rate deficit for the dollar, but SOFR at 3.88% combined with broader dollar demand overrides the NOK carry advantage. Retail positioning displays a 91% long bias on USD/NOK, presenting extreme retail crowding. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK, driven by broad USD outperformance and geopolitical shipping risk. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Sharp de-escalation in Hormuz shipping risks combined with Brent crude surging above $90/bbl forces a repricing in favor of NOK.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium + Geopolitical Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.84, holding above its SMA20 at 158.03 and SMA200 at 158.69 while hovering just below the critical 160.00 intervention threshold. OIS carry basis shows SOFR at 3.88% vs TONA at 1.23%, delivering a +265bp yield spread that strongly supports the dollar against the yen. Options market pricing reflects severe downside hedging demand, with the 1M 25-delta Risk Reversal printing a strong put skew of -1.87 despite COT Leveraged Funds holding a net short JPY position of -21,213 contracts (92nd percentile). BoJ board member Asada reiterated caution on aggressive hikes, keeping real policy rates deeply negative at -2.25%. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while VIX remains contained at 17.5. Catalyst: US PPI release at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Direct intervention by the Ministry of Finance or a sustained spot break above 160.00 triggers immediate official yen-buying operations.

signals.title: EUR/USD — BEER Model Cheapness vs Downtrend
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1080, maintaining its position below the SMA20 (1.1193), SMA50 (1.1320), and SMA200 (1.1535) moving average cluster. The OIS spread has SOFR at 3.88% vs €STR at 2.44%, giving USD a +144bp carry advantage that continues to suppress spot. COT Leveraged Funds report net short EUR positioning of -104,030 contracts (2nd percentile, z = -1.80), marking an extreme speculative short stretch. Equilibrium valuation metrics show EUR/USD at a BEER misvaluation z-score of -3.50σ (cheap vs fair value at 1.1252), while retail sentiment sits at 89% long. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, constrained by multi-month downtrend structure and carry deficit. Catalyst: Euro Area GDP q/q print at 10:00 UTC. Risk: ECB President Lagarde speech at 19:30 UTC signals hawkish policy pivot, prompting a short-squeeze across stretched speculative shorts.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Q3 GDP Beat vs Moving Average Cluster
signals.text: GBP/USD prints at 1.3260, trading below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 1.3368, SMA200 at 1.3417) following UK Q3 GDP growth accelerating to 0.7% qoq. OIS benchmarks list SONIA at 3.98% vs SOFR at 3.88%, establishing a modest +10bp carry advantage for sterling while BoE policy rate at 4.00% matches the Fed. COT Leveraged Funds net long GBP stands at +32,686 contracts (65th percentile), reflecting steady institutional backing even as 25d Risk Reversals indicate a mild put skew of -0.50. Economic Surprise Index for GBP sits at +4.1, reflecting balanced macroeconomic releases. Trade bias: Neutral/cautious GBP/USD, evaluating counter-trend bounce momentum against structural technical resistance. Catalyst: US Existing Home Sales at 15:00 UTC. Risk: Technical rejection at the 1.3325 resistance zone reinstates broad dollar downside pressure.

signals.title: AUD/USD — OIS Carry Advantage vs Technical Weakness
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6827, remaining below its SMA20 (0.6977) and SMA200 (0.7058) in a extended downtrend 2.68 ATR from its 20-day moving average. The RBA policy rate at 4.85% vs Fed at 4.00% yields a +85bp nominal policy rate differential, while OIS basis places AONIA at 4.85% vs SOFR at 3.88%, creating a +97bp carry advantage in favor of AUD. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold a net long position of +43,532 contracts (46th percentile), while retail trader positioning displays a 71% long allocation. Australia's ESI prints at -5.5, pointing to moderate economic data disappointments. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, macro carry support offset by deteriorating risk-appetite and technical momentum. Catalyst: Federal Reserve Governor Bowman speech at 15:50 UTC. Risk: Broad commodity rebound drives spot recovery back toward the 0.6905 resistance level.
